safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 3.0 to 1.77 days

narrative: Demand for PL1__MF3DD6BA is near-continuous and moderately variable (CV=39%, mean 66.6 units/day) with no detectable trend over the 197 working-day horizon. Lead times are highly volatile (CV=97%), showing a bimodal pattern of fast (~0.8 day) and slow (~3 day) deliveries, which is the dominant risk driver for buffer sizing. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock raised from 95 to 118 units and an EOQ-driven order quantity of 1,185 units is recommended, cutting total annual inventory cost by 66.4% while meeting the 95% service level and remaining well within the 1,908-unit storage cap.
warnings: Lead time CV=97% is high; bimodal supplier behaviour detected — monitor for structural shift
EOQ (1,185) significantly exceeds MOQ (190); verify supplier accepts large infrequent orders

research_insights.selection_rationale: Near-continuous demand with moderate CV suits a continuous-review reorder-point trigger; the fixed EOQ batch amortises the $50 ordering cost efficiently and avoids the excess stock of a periodic policy under volatile lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap (1,908 units) is non-binding: SS(118)+OQ(1,185)=1,303 units = 68.3% utilisation. No capacity-driven reduction applied.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ(190)+SS(118)=308 units well below max_storage_units(1,908); policy is fully feasible
